papers.title: TEFAR: a lightweight, configurable framework for semi-automatic artefact component classification in EEG and TMS-EEG
papers.summary: TEFAR is a lightweight, configurable FieldTrip-based framework for semi-automatic artefact component classification in EEG and TMS-EEG, using robust statistics and signature-based detectors for artefacts including TMS decay and recharge. In 30 ground-truth simulations, it achieved specificity of 1.000 and sensitivity of 0.96-0.97 for both profiles.

papers.title: Aperiodic dynamics track cortical state shifts during sleep K-complexes
papers.summary: Using time-resolved spectral parameterization of overnight sleep EEG, this study characterized aperiodic dynamics around expert-annotated K-complexes and applied controls to separate genuine state changes from waveform artifacts. A component of the KC-locked change in the aperiodic exponent survived these controls, suggesting K-complexes are accompanied by a shift toward a higher-exponent, inhibition-dominated cortical state, while also highlighting measurement confounds for event-locked spectral analyses of large transients.

papers.title: EMA-Based Subspace Tracking for Adaptive Artifact Subspace Reconstruction
papers.summary: The paper proposes EMA-based adaptive subspace tracking for Artifact Subspace Reconstruction (ASR), integrating short-horizon covariance estimation with slow recursive assimilation to handle non-stationary EEG. On 24-channel EEG from 10 subjects, EMA-ASR achieved 53.1% blink reduction versus 24.0% and 26.7% for Original and memory-limited ASR, with increased reconstruction and spectral deviation.

papers.title: Separating personal from population gains when calibrating EEG foundation models for new users
papers.summary: The paper evaluates personal adaptation of three frozen EEG foundation models (CBraMod, REVE, LaBraM) in 235 held-out subjects across three motor-imagery datasets, comparing adapters against population models and exchanged adapters. Personal adapters improved mean balanced accuracy by 1.5–5.4 percentage points over the population model and by 2.3–7.3 points over exchanged adapters in all nine model-dataset combinations.

papers.title: Tutorial on using EEG microstates to study moment-to-moment large-scale functional brain network dynamics in neurodevelopment.
papers.summary: This tutorial provides a practical guide to EEG microstate analysis for developmental populations, focusing on special considerations for high-artifact data within the HAPPE software. It details conceptual foundations, a step-by-step pipeline for resting-state and task-based EEG, and provides freely available datasets and annotated code to make microstate computation accessible and reproducible.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for EEG Decoding: How Much Data Is Enough?
papers.summary: The study investigates scaling laws for EEG decoding by evaluating five models across four datasets, manipulating training data volume via subject count and trial volume under cross-subject validation, and fitting power-law relationships. It finds that as total data volume increases, the distinction between trial and subject scaling becomes largely irrelevant, and power-law relationships are model- and dataset-specific but provide a robust descriptive framework, with extrapolation yielding RMSE below 0.1 in most cases.

papers.title: Intermittent Cranial Accelerometric Pulses - a Potential Marker of Neurodegenerative Disease
papers.summary: This preprint identifies a novel phenomenon of brief periodic 'Sleep Bursts' in cranial forces during human sleep, occurring less frequently in subjects with neurodegenerative disease. EEG delta power during bursts was significantly lower in NDD subjects, suggesting a potential glymphatic drainage marker.

papers.title: Resting state EEG microstates: is a new FORM all you need?
papers.summary: The authors introduce First-Order spherical haRMonic (FORM), a fixed three-dimensional geometry defined only by sensor positions, to describe EEG scalp topographies independently of any microstate clustering solution. FORM explained 0.966-0.998 of energy for canonical microstate maps, preserved literature template organization (Spearman rho = 0.987), and FORM conformity explained a median 74.4% of within-subject variance in winning-template correlation in continuous EEG, versus 21.7% for GFP.

papers.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Why Representation Matters for Biological Interpretation in Dementia EEG
papers.summary: The paper examines how dementia-associated EEG entropy differences depend on permutation-entropy representation, analyzing 1,177 CAUEEG alpha-band recordings under four PE settings and nine processing specifications. It finds that dementia PE contrasts reversed sign depending on representation (original d=-0.690 to +0.705; sub-cycle negative d=-0.729 to -0.576; coarse-sampled positive +0.625 to +0.712), indicating that biological interpretation requires justified connections between signal distinctions and brain dynamics.

papers.title: EEGDM: Label-Efficient EEG Representation Learning with Generative Diffusion Model.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: EEGDM is a diffusion-based EEG representation learning framework that uses a Structured State-Space Model for Diffusion Pretraining and a Latent Fusion Module for downstream tasks. It achieved competitive or superior performance to state-of-the-art methods on EEG event classification, seizure detection, and seizure classification benchmarks while requiring substantially fewer samples for pretraining and adaptation.

papers.title: Validation of an EEG-based Delirium Monitor in the ICU
papers.summary: This multicenter prospective cohort study monitored 225 adult ICU patients with the Ceribell point-of-care EEG system to validate its ability to detect delirium against expert clinician diagnoses and CAM-ICU assessments. The EEG system detected delirium with 81% sensitivity and 81% specificity, and its continuous score correlated with CAM-ICU-7 severity scores (median rho 0.58).

papers.title: When Is an SAE Feature Interpretable? A Validation Ladder for EEG Foundation Models
papers.summary: Across 27 settings spanning three EEG backbones and datasets, alpha-band removal changed sparse autoencoder latent firing 7.3 times more than a sham notch, but after normalizing by removed spectral energy the ratio fell to 0.28 and never exceeded one, and selected latents were slightly anti-correlated with relative alpha power on clean EEG. The authors propose a validation ladder for semantic interpretations of SAE latents, showing that perturbation sensitivity alone does not establish what a latent represents.

papers.title: A Patient-Specific Framework for Separating Temporal Localization from Intracranial Waveform Reconstruction of Interictal Epileptiform Discharges from Scalp EEG
papers.summary: A patient-specific dual-branch convolutional-attention framework separated temporal localization from event-specific intracranial waveform reconstruction of interictal epileptiform discharges using simultaneous scalp and intracranial EEG in six subjects. Scalp EEG supported temporal localization above chance in three of six subjects, but event-specific waveform reconstruction was not consistently better than a fixed patient-specific template.

papers.title: Identifying Neural Source Dynamics from Unknown Local Interventions
papers.summary: The paper shows that unknown local changes to source update rules can identify EEG source dynamics, leaving a rank-one source-specific signature that is isolated by subtracting matched baseline responses and localized via the forward model. Under sufficient recovery conditions, combining these intervention histories with initialization responses recovers all source interactions without baseline reachability, and simulated EEG on MRI-derived anatomy recovered all dynamics in 32/32 systems with eight unknown changes.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for ATN Classification in Early Alzheimer's disease
papers.summary: EEG was recorded in 60 participants with SCD, MCI-, and MCI+ across task and resting-state paradigms, and event-related, spectral, connectivity, and complexity features were related to CSF/plasma ATN biomarkers and classification. EEG uniquely separated SCD from MCI (AUC approximately 0.72-0.75) where plasma biomarkers failed (AUC approximately 0.32-0.33), while plasma pTau217 performed near ceiling for ATN-based discrimination (AUC 0.96-0.99).

papers.title: Pre-treatment EEG microstates and response to antipsychotic drugs in first episode psychosis
papers.summary: In 56 minimally treated first-episode psychosis patients, baseline resting-state EEG microstate PC1 predicted 12-week antipsychotic treatment response (adjusted OR=0.63, AUC=72.3% with clinical information). Microstate architecture deviating from a healthy-control-derived norm was associated with lower odds of treatment response.

papers.title: Current knowledge of intermittent photic stimulation for electroencephalography in dogs.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge of intermittent photic stimulation for EEG in dogs, showing that protocols vary substantially in stimulus design, vigilance state, and electrode montage. It proposes a framework for standardized awake testing and improved spatial sampling to enhance diagnostic sensitivity and translational alignment.

papers.title: Decoding obstructive sleep apnea phenotypes through integrated multimodal sleep EEG.
papers.summary: Integrating multimodal sleep EEG, clinical, and biomarker data from 309 OSA patients via a cascaded multimodal transformer and consensus clustering identified three stable neurophysiological phenotypes that were all discriminated by qEEG-derived features. Mean AHI did not differ significantly across phenotypes, but AHI severity category distributions did, demonstrating a dissociation between conventional severity metrics and neurophysiological subtypes.

papers.title: Boundary conditions for cortical speech tracking as an objective speech-in-noise marker: a three-dataset MEG/EEG benchmark.
papers.summary: Using three public MEG/EEG datasets, this benchmark tested cortical speech tracking as a speech-in-noise marker, finding delta-band envelope reconstruction increased with intelligibility at the group level but individual neurometric SRTs showed limited agreement with behavioral SRTs (r=0.29). Attended speech was tracked more strongly than ignored speech, yet EEG markers produced only small model-dependent predictive gains, indicating group-level condition and attention sensitivity but protocol-dependent individual SRT translation.

papers.title: Binary Classification of Consciousness Using Cerebral Blood Flow and EEG Features.
papers.summary: Retrospectively analyzed 26 adults with severe brain injury to test whether combining cerebral blood flow features with EEG improves binary classification of consciousness. A random forest model using EEG alpha-delta ratio, total EEG power, and CBF bands IV and V achieved ROC-AUC 0.86 and accuracy 82%, outperforming EEG-only models.

papers.title: Cortical Spectral Dynamics in Flow and Frustration
papers.summary: EEG data from ten adults performing go and stop-signal tasks with continuously adjusted difficulty were analyzed for spectral dynamics during flow versus frustration, alongside subjective flow ratings. In the flow block, stop-trial errors coincided with pre-stimulus reductions in right temporoparietal gamma power, frontal beta and gamma power, and frontotemporal gamma coherence, while frustration showed higher temporal beta power.

papers.title: Subregion-specific temporal lobe EEG signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: Evidence from high-density EEG.
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state 128-channel high-density EEG in 55 individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and 35 cognitively normal controls to characterize temporal-subregional electrophysiological features. Individuals with aMCI showed increased gamma-band activity across bilateral temporal subregions, elevated delta power and theta/beta ratios mainly in right temporal subregions, enhanced fast-frequency coupling, and gamma measures from left temporal subregions achieved discriminatory performance comparable to whole-temporal measures.

papers.title: Multidimensional EEG mechanisms and explainable prediction of responsiveness to posterior parietal HD-tDCS in chronic disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Applied HD-tDCS over Pz to 42 patients with chronic disorders of consciousness and analyzed resting-state EEG using spectral parameterization, nonlinear complexity, and recurrence quantification. Responders showed decreased aperiodic exponent, increased 20-35 Hz power and normalized spatial complexity, and an explainable machine learning model identified these as predictive features.

papers.title: Longitudinal adaptations in neural and behavioral systems following hearing restoration using cochlear implants.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This longitudinal study followed 19 newly implanted adult cochlear implant users over 12 months, measuring speech recognition, spatial hearing, quality of life, and EEG neural tracking during a continuous-speech selective-attention task. Speech recognition and spatial-separation benefits improved, task-relevant neural tracking was stronger and earlier than task-irrelevant tracking, and stronger task-relevant tracking correlated with better speech recognition, spatial listening, and quality of life, with gains plateauing by about 6 months.

papers.title: 30 Hz High-Definition Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation at the Left Frontal Cortex Reduces the Spectral Slope of the EEG in the Contralateral Hemisphere
papers.summary: Analyzed EEG from 9 participants during a compensatory tracking task across sessions with 30 Hz HD-tACS over left motor or frontal cortex, isolating the aperiodic spectral slope. Frontal HD-tACS decreased the spectral slope in the right frontal cortex, and pre-stimulation spectral slope correlated with task accuracy changes, suggesting a screening biomarker.

papers.title: Continuous Versus Routine EEG in Critically Ill Patients Without Primary Neurologic Condition: Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a post hoc analysis of the multicenter randomized CERTA trial restricted to 76 critically ill adults without primary neurologic conditions, continuous EEG was not associated with 6-month mortality, functional outcome, seizure detection, or medication changes compared with two routine EEG recordings. No seizures or status epilepticus were detected in either group, suggesting repeated routine EEG may be a reasonable alternative in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers During Upper-Limb Action Observation Therapy for Stroke Rehabilitation: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review identified 22 studies combining upper-limb action observation therapy with EEG outcomes and motor assessments after stroke. Sensorimotor event-related desynchronization in mu (8-13 Hz) and beta (13-30 Hz) bands consistently indexed action observation network engagement, and multi-week interventions produced sustained increases in mu/beta ERD and beta connectivity that frequently correlated with Fugl-Meyer, dexterity, and functional improvements, though protocol heterogeneity limits cross-study comparability.

papers.title: Aberrant Neural Outputs and Disrupted Neural Oscillations of the Cerebellar Nuclei in a Mouse Model of Fragile X Syndrome.
papers.summary: Using Fmr1-knockout mice, this study mapped deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) projections and recorded in vivo electrophysiology to examine cerebellar output in Fragile X syndrome. It found target-specific alterations in DCN forebrain projections, disrupted neuronal firing patterns, loss of specific neuronal subtypes, and aberrant local field potential oscillations with weakened theta, alpha, and beta power despite unchanged gamma power, without morphological changes.

papers.title: Electrophysiological brain reconfiguration during meditation-induced extended cessation of consciousness: an EEG microstate study
papers.summary: This EEG microstate study examined five highly trained meditators during meditation-induced extended cessation (EC) of consciousness and compared it with counting and memory tasks. EC was associated with reduced microstate B (self-related processing), increased microstate C (integrative activity), and preferential routing of sensory-related microstate A toward integrative rather than self-related processing, indicating a distinct neural signature of transiently suspended consciousness.

papers.title: Automated Cerebral Edema Detection using Electroencephalography in Post-cardiac Arrest Patients.
papers.summary: Developed transformer and LSTM machine learning models to detect diffuse cerebral edema from routine EEG in post-cardiac arrest patients and to predict edema before radiographic detection. A transformer using 4-hour EEG segments achieved median AUC 83.5%, and a prediction model using 8-hour segments achieved median AUC 80.0%.

papers.title: Mu suppression reveals auditory-motor predictions after short musical training.
papers.summary: Twenty-five non-musicians learned a simple melody on a piano-like keyboard while EEG was recorded, then passively listened to trained and control melodies before and after training. Mu suppression emerged before each note only for the practiced melody after training, indicating that short motor training supports single-note-level auditory-motor predictions independent of prior musical experience.

papers.title: AAV-mediated TBR1 supplementation ameliorates behavioral and electrophysiological abnormalities in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice
papers.summary: This study tested AAV-mediated human TBR1 supplementation in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice via retroorbital injection at postnatal day 3, assessing protein levels, cell counts, behavior, and EEG. Treatment increased TBR1 protein and TBR1-, CTIP2-, and parvalbumin-positive cell counts, improved sociability and food-seeking behaviors, and attenuated elevated relative theta power and improved theta suppression and gamma enhancement during social interaction, although some anatomical and EEG abnormalities persisted.

papers.title: Semantic distance differently modulates FPVS-EEG responses to words and pictures
papers.summary: Using fast periodic visual stimulation EEG in 24 healthy subjects, the study showed that semantic distance between concepts modulates 1-Hz responses to pictures and words differently: pictures elicited larger amplitudes for high- versus low-distance conditions, whereas words showed a reversed pattern. The findings support a similarity-based structure of semantic representations and differential mapping between semantic and surface representations.

papers.title: Early EEG responses indicate liking for artworks presented in rapid visual streams
papers.summary: Using EEG and representational similarity analysis in two rapid serial visual presentation experiments (300 ms and 50 ms SOA) with 999 artworks, the study found that neural responses within the first 150 ms predicted liking similarity even without liking judgments. This early automatic EEG correlate of liking was robust across both presentation speeds, indicating that the perceptual basis of art liking emerges in a split second.

papers.title: Predicting the immediate and subsequent effects of commercials on product valuation using EEG and deep learning
papers.summary: This neuromarketing study recorded EEG from 161 participants while they viewed commercials and measured willingness to pay (WTP) immediately and one week later. Deep learning models applied to raw EEG achieved substantially higher predictive accuracy than standard EEG measures, successfully predicting immediate and delayed WTP and ad liking, including for new participants and products, though accuracy declined with increasing generalization demands and narrower value differences.

papers.title: GRASP: a response-locked paradigm that reveals low-beta desynchronisation is a participant-invariant signature of semantic decoding in EEG.
papers.summary: Introducing GRASP, a response-locked auditory paradigm with pseudo-word dummy trials, the study found that meaningful concept retrieval versus pseudo-word recognition produced participant-invariant low-beta EEG desynchronisation peaking around 15 Hz in all 13 participants and all three semantic categories. This low-beta signature is proposed as a stable electrophysiological target for semantic brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title: Distinct hierarchical effects of goal specificity and reward uncertainty on decision-making: An active inference EEG-fNIRS study.
papers.summary: Combining EEG-fNIRS with active inference modeling during a probabilistic reversal learning task, the study found that specific goal setting improved accuracy and was linked to more stable top-down policy selection, including choice-locked P3 modulations, reduced centro-parietal beta desynchronisation, and increased DLPFC HbO entropy. Reward uncertainty was primarily associated with bottom-up belief updating, reflected in belief-entropy effects on feedback-locked P3b and greater fronto-parietal global efficiency under high uncertainty.

papers.title: Viral Strategies for In Vivo Optogenetic Stimulation of Purkinje Cell Terminals and Electrophysiological Characterization of Downstream Cerebellar Nuclear Activity in Mice
papers.summary: This methods paper describes two viral strategies for expressing the fast channelrhodopsin ChETA in cerebellar Purkinje cells to enable in vivo optogenetic activation of their axonal terminals in the medial deep cerebellar nuclei of mice. Using in vivo extracellular electrophysiology, the authors demonstrate light-evoked modulation of downstream cerebellar nuclear activity, providing a reproducible protocol for cell-type-specific manipulation of cerebellar circuits.

papers.title: Moderate prenatal alcohol exposure differentially alters acute ethanol sensitivity of GABAergic transmission in CRFR1- and CRFR1+ CeM Neurons.
papers.summary: Using CRF1-Cre-tdTomato rats, this study examined how moderate prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) alters acute ethanol modulation of GABAergic transmission onto CRFR1+ and CRFR1- neurons in the adult central amygdala. Whole-cell electrophysiology revealed cell type- and concentration-dependent effects that differed by sex, suggesting PAE dysregulates acute ethanol's modulation of GABA transmission in a sex-specific manner.

papers.title: Spectral Analysis of the T Cell Repertoire Recovery Following Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplantation
papers.summary: The study applied Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to TRB V gene segment clonal frequencies from 12 allogeneic stem cell transplant donors and recipients, revealing donor spectral peaks at 113–335 millicycles/kb. PT-CY recipients showed donor-like spectra, whereas ATG recipients had dispersed spectra with a centroid shift to higher frequencies and reduced low-frequency indices, suggesting PT-CY better preserves normal TRB V segment organization.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
